proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the series exhibits meaningful within-season immunity waning or multi-wave behavior, SEIR may underfit late-season rebounds and compensate via inflated transmission/initial conditions.
proposals.rationale: Use a parsimonious SEIR backbone with a short (1-week) reporting/clinical lag to represent hospitalization-rate measurement as a lagged incidence proxy, while avoiding the added flexibility of waning immunity that may drive split-sensitive behavior.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the hospitalization signal is better captured by prevalence-like dynamics rather than lagged incidence, delayed_I may misalign peak timing/width and produce systematic phase error.
proposals.rationale: Keep the lagged-incidence observation aligned with prior best delay while simplifying dynamics (no S->R->S loop) to improve rolling-split stability and reduce sensitivity to validation-window placement.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Longer delay can induce overly late peaks and may force the model to shift epidemic timing earlier than plausible, harming early-season rolling forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Test the upper end of the constrained lag range to capture longer admission delays without adding compartments; useful given mild delay sensitivity and high rate scale where timing errors dominate.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Extra flexibility from waning immunity may still be weakly identified in 31 training weeks, leading to parameter tradeoffs that vary across rolling windows.
proposals.rationale: Retain SEIRS to allow modest waning immunity while using a shorter lag to reduce the tendency for SEIRS(delay=2) to overfit a particular split; aims for better rolling-only consistency.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May exacerbate identifiability issues (waning vs timing) and yield unstable peak placement across rolling splits.
proposals.rationale: Complement the prior SEIRS(delay=2) best spec by bracketing with a longer lag to check whether split sensitivity is tied to the specific delay choice versus the SEIRS structure itself.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H dynamics may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, causing unstable H/I partitioning and inconsistent rolling forecasts despite similar in-sample fit.
proposals.rationale: Include one explicit hospitalization compartment with direct H observation to better match the target semantics (hospitalization rate) while keeping the mapping simple (no aggregation) to limit under-identification.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is truly admissions-only, I+H can bias amplitude/shape (too smooth or too large), and the model may misattribute signal between I and H.
proposals.rationale: Use I+H observation as a robust proxy when the reported hospitalization rate may reflect a mixture of infectious prevalence and admissions (e.g., ascertainment/definition drift), potentially improving rolling stability versus pure H.
